picks.intervention_label: Active surveillance — structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years then space out; no adjuvant systemic therapy
picks.rationale: With no measurable disease and a tumor this indolent, there is nothing for an adjuvant regimen to act on, so the tolerability side of the patient's 0.65 weight wins by default. Boikos 2016 puts imatinib at a 2% response rate in this subset, and both NCCN and ESMO say it plainly: no adjuvant TKI here. Surveillance also keeps every recurrence contingency open instead of spending trial-screening eligibility on a regimen the biology rejects. The one axis it does not fully satisfy is prefers_trials, since surveillance is not a trial, which is exactly why the registry sits right behind it.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight 0.65: satisfied — no chronic toxicity committed where there is no efficacy to gain
prefers_trials: in tension — surveillance is not a trial; the registry pick is the mitigation
no toxicity vetoes or modality constraints were stated, so there is nothing to clear on those axes

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) + cancer-genetics counseling for the SDHA germline result and POLE R1679C reclassification
picks.rationale: This is the one move that honors prefers_trials today. The patient is NED, which locks them out of nearly every contingency trial that needs measurable disease, but the NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study takes them as they are, at zero toxicity. It also banks tissue, opens the SDHC-methylation fallback if the SDHA workup wobbles, and pairs cleanly with the genetics counseling the germline question already demands. For a trial-preferring patient with nothing to enroll on, this is as close as it gets right now.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials: fully satisfied — the only enrollable trial while the patient is NED
efficacy/tox weight: satisfied — zero toxicity
preferences are defaulted, not elicited; travel tolerance for the NIH baseline visit should be confirmed before this is leaned on

picks.intervention_label: SDHA germline panel + SDHA/SDHB IHC re-cut with internal control + tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants
picks.rationale: Every dSDH-GIST trial the patient might want later gates on SDHB-IHC loss, and the report has SDHB reading intact against a biallelic SDHA call, and that discrepancy could quietly disqualify them at screening. One tissue pull answers three things: germline versus somatic SDHA (cascade testing and lifelong PGL surveillance ride on it), whether the SDHA IHC reconciles the paradox, and whether the ctDNA-only variants are real in tumor. There is no therapeutic toxicity, and it protects the trial eligibility the patient says they want. The cost is a few weeks of turnaround before any recurrence plan can move.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials: protected — confirms the SDHB-loss phenotype every contingency trial screens on
efficacy/tox weight: neutral — diagnostic, no therapeutic effect
tension: if the SDHA IHC also reads intact, the dSDH label collapses and the trial route narrows

picks.intervention_label: Paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma baseline surveillance — plasma free metanephrines (LC-MS/MS) + rapid-sequence whole-body MRI; Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT reserved for baseline + change-flagging
picks.rationale: An SDHx carrier with an undetected functional paraganglioma who goes under anesthesia for a future re-resection is a hypertensive crisis waiting to happen, and this patient may well face more surgery. One plasma metanephrines draw plus a whole-body MRI sets the clean baseline now, so later the question becomes what changed rather than whether a comparator exists. It is non-invasive, carries no therapeutic toxicity, and runs into no stated preference. Cadence tightens or relaxes once the germline SDHA result is back.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight: satisfied — non-invasive, no therapeutic toxicity
no preference conflict elicited or apparent
annual-versus-biennial cadence is unresolved until the germline result returns

picks.intervention_label: Signatera tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay as a recurrence-surveillance adjunct to imaging (informative, not therapy-triggering)
picks.rationale: The patient has detectable SDHA, PIK3CA, and MAP2K1 variants in plasma pre-resection, so a tumor-informed assay is genuinely informative for this individual rather than a generic add-on. Signatera can give lead-time over imaging, with one hard guardrail: a positive result buys a shorter-interval scan, not a TKI. It is venipuncture only, so it sits fine against the tolerability weight. The GIST-specific validation is thinner than colorectal or lung, so I would frame it as informative, not therapy-triggering.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight: satisfied — venipuncture only
prefers_trials: partial — an adjunct to a trial-aware plan, not itself a trial
a ctDNA-positive / imaging-negative result is a counseling trap; the imaging guardrail is load-bearing

picks.intervention_label: Recurrence contingency — trial-route first (olverembatinib NCT06640361, belzutifan NCT04924075, pemigatinib/PEMIGIST NCT07434843, temozolomide NCT05661643) with sunitinib as the FDA-approved co-equal fallback
picks.rationale: At first measurable recurrence, prefers_trials says the trial menu gets presented alongside sunitinib, not behind it. The freshest data back that: olverembatinib now has a real dSDH-GIST readout (ORR 23.1%, mPFS 25.7 mo) and is recruiting, belzutifan carries the cleanest mechanism case with 14 US sites open, and pemigatinib rides the rogaratinib signal (ORR 41.7%), though rogaratinib's own trial has closed to accrual, so that specific door is shut. Sunitinib stays the FDA-approved fallback (Boikos 18% ORR in this subset), best offered as a co-equal option rather than the default first reach. Which trial actually fits turns on geography and the dSDH confirmation, neither of which has been elicited yet.
primary_concerns: prefers_trials: satisfied at recurrence — the trial menu is presented alongside, not behind, sunitinib
efficacy/tox weight 0.65: mostly satisfied — oral agents, but real chronic AE profiles (belzutifan anemia compounded by Roux-en-Y; FGFR-class retinal and phosphate monitoring)
tension: geography and dSDH confirmation are unelicited and gate which trial is reachable

picks.intervention_label: Adjuvant imatinib — NOT RECOMMENDED in dSDH-GIST (logged as a veto so the no-imatinib call is documented and not re-litigated)
picks.rationale: I am logging this as a veto so the reflex GIST-means-imatinib reach gets documented and is not re-litigated on the post-op note. In this subset imatinib runs a 2% response rate (Boikos 2016) and ESMO 2022 recommends against it outright. Three years of edema, fatigue, and monitoring burden against a 2% return fails the tolerability weight under any reading, and it would spend the screening eligibility for the contingency trials the patient prefers. With no efficacy to lean on, there is no version of the 0.65 weight that rescues this.
primary_concerns: efficacy/tox weight: fails outright — 2% response against three years of toxicity
prefers_trials: fails — not a trial, and it burns trial-screening eligibility
logged as a veto on the patient's behalf

notes: Worth saying plainly: this patient gave no preferences, so everything above runs on defaults. The 0.65 weight and prefers_trials=true are reasonable stand-ins, but I would want both confirmed before any of this hardens, especially scan-anxiety tolerance (the real cost of indefinite surveillance, and nobody has asked) and travel range (which decides whether the registry visit and the recurrence trials are even reachable). The defaults happen to land on the same answer the guidelines give, but that is convergence, not elicitation.
